What object are we constructing, what information does it retain, and what scientific claim could it support?

## Where Week 5 sits

Weeks 2–4: inspect the construction by hand.

Week 5: carry out and audit an end-to-end computation.

$$
\text{stored data}\to\text{filtered object}\to
\text{software output}\to\text{checked interpretation}.
$$

The data object comes first; the complex follows.

---

## The practical audit loop

1. Inspect the stored object and units.
2. Predict visible topology and its plausible scale.
3. Construct and count the filtered object.
4. Compute with explicit conventions.
5. Check one small result by hand.
6. Change one decision at a time.
7. Report a qualified interpretation.

---

## Method map

| Starting object | Core construction | Parameter |
|---|---|---|
| Point cloud or distances | Rips | pairwise threshold |
| Weighted graph | graph or clique complex | edge weight |
| Scalar grid | cubical complex | cell value |
| Values on complex vertices | lower star | vertex-derived value |

The Interlude contains the broader menu. This week practises three routes deeply
enough to audit their implementation.

---

## Computational cautions

Rips complexes grow quickly. For an $N$-point cloud, the Vietoris–Rips
filtration contains $O(N^2)$ edges, $O(N^3)$ triangles, $O(N^4)$
tetrahedra and so on. Even when truncating at dimension 2, the size can
scale like $O(N^3)$. This is why the choice of maximum dimension,
maximum filtration value and sparsification strategy is not merely
technical.

---

## The cost of asking for higher homology

| Request | Must construct through | Worst-case count |
|---|---|---:|
| $H_0$ | edges | $\binom N2$ |
| $H_1$ | triangles | $\binom N3$ |
| $H_2$ | tetrahedra | $\binom N4$ |
| $H_p$ | $(p+1)$-simplices | $\binom N{p+2}$ |

$$C_{p+1}\xrightarrow{\partial_{p+1}}C_p
\xrightarrow{\partial_p}C_{p-1}.$$

To know whether a $p$-cycle is filled, the computation needs the next
dimension.

---

## A dangerous truncation

Requesting `max_dimension=1` may display graph cycles but omit the triangles
that should kill them.

For correct $H_1$, construct through dimension 2.

For correct $H_2$, construct through dimension 3.

Dimensions above $p+1$ cannot change $H_p$ and consume unnecessary memory.

---

## One stack, three implementation clinics

| Input | Construction | Filtration value |
|---|---|---|
| Point cloud | Rips complex | Distance threshold |
| Weighted graph | Graph or clique complex | Edge weight |
| Scalar grid | Cubical complex | Cell value |

The common software does not make these the same mathematical object.

---

## Cubical means filled grid cells

![](../../assets/week05-cubical-sublevel.svg){fig-alt="A scalar grid enters as filled square cells. Low-valued cells form a ring and the central high-valued cell later fills its hole." height="280"}

Each pixel is a square 2-cell. Its edges and vertices enter with it.

Birth and death coordinates are field values, not distances.

---

## Where do the scalar values live?

Lower star: values begin on vertices.

Cubical practical: values begin on top-dimensional grid cells.

State the convention before interpreting birth.

Alpha complexes are optional, not part of the core practical.

---

## Sensitivity or a new question?

Subsample the same point cloud: sensitivity check.

Fill graph cliques: new higher-order assumption.

Negate a scalar field: switch from low-valued to high-valued structure.

::: {.sticking}
**▶ Likely sticking point.** Not every software setting is a harmless tuning parameter.
:::

---

## Weighted graph walkthrough

Graph only:

$$[0.45,\infty),\qquad[0.85,\infty).$$

Clique expansion adds filled triangles at 0.45 and 0.85, so both cycles are
born and filled at the same parameter value. No positive-length $H_1$ bars
remain.

Same weighted edges; different higher-order representation.

---

## Scalar-image walkthrough

$$f(x,y)=(x^2+y^2-1)^2.$$

Low-valued pixels form an annular band.

Computed main interval:

$$[0.0055,1.0000).$$

Birth reflects grid discretisation near the unit circle. Death occurs when the
high-valued centre enters and fills the opening.

## Computational reporting

State data dimensions and units, preprocessing, metric or cell convention,
complex, parameter meaning, coefficient field, maximum dimension and
threshold, simplex or cell counts, software version, runtime and memory
failures.
